t.7.48.1: Seeing Sītā weeping, the sons of the sages who were there ran to the place where the blessed Vālmīki, of foremost intellect, was seated.
t.7.48.2: Having saluted the sage's feet, all the sons of the sages reported to the great seer the sound of her weeping.
t.7.48.3: O blessed one, this woman, never seen before, the wife of some great-souled man, like Śrī herself, is wailing in a distorted voice out of bewilderment.
t.7.48.4: O revered one, look well at this woman, who is like a goddess fallen from the sky. Indeed, we do not take her to be a mortal woman; let due honour be shown to her.
t.7.48.5: Having heard those words of theirs and having ascertained the matter through his understanding, the knower of dharma, endowed with the vision gained through austerity, hastened to where Maithilī was.
t.7.48.6: The great sage, setting out for that place a short way on foot and taking with him a beautiful guest-offering, reached the bank of the Jāhnavī, and there he saw Sītā, the beloved wife of Rāghava, looking like one without a protector.
t.7.48.7: To Sītā, afflicted by the burden of grief, Vālmīki, the foremost of sages, spoke sweet words, as though gladdening her with his radiance.
t.7.48.8: You are the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, the virtuous chief queen of Rāma, and the daughter of King Janaka; welcome to you, O devoted wife!
t.7.48.9: Even as you were approaching, you were recognized by me through meditation upon dharma; and the whole cause of your coming has been perceived by my heart.
t.7.48.10: O Sītā, with the eye gained through austerity I know you to be sinless. O Vaidehī, you who are pure of heart now dwell with me.
t.7.48.11: Not far from my hermitage dwell female ascetics devoted to austerity; they, my child, will always care for you as a cow cares for her calf.
t.7.48.12: Accept this guest-offering, trusting and free from anxiety; as though you had come to your own home, do not give way to dejection.
t.7.48.13: Having heard the sage's most wonderful speech, Sītā bowed her head to his feet and, with joined palms, said, "So be it."
t.7.48.14: Sītā, her hands joined in reverence, followed behind the sage as he went on; she followed him to the place where the female ascetics dwelt, ever devoted to dharma and composed in mind.
t.7.48.15: Then, seeing the sage approaching, followed by Vaidehī, the women came up to him filled with joy and spoke these words.
t.7.48.17: Having heard those words of theirs, Vālmīki said this: "This is Sītā, the wife of the wise Rāma, who has arrived here."
t.7.48.16: Welcome to you, best of sages! Your coming is after a long time, lord. We all salute you; let it be told what we should do.
t.7.48.18: This woman, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha and the daughter of Janaka, a virtuous and sinless lady abandoned by her husband, must always be protected by me.
t.7.48.19: Let you ladies look upon her with the greatest affection; out of regard for my word, let her be especially honoured by you.
t.7.48.20: Having comforted Vaidehī again and again, the greatly renowned one of great austerity, surrounded by his disciples, returned once more to his own hermitage.
